The setupSuppose one person, with no formal training in mathematics or academic writing, produces the following in under a year: a dystopian novel, several research-style papers with stability theorems, a dissertation-style manuscript with a bibliography, a lexicon of roughly two hundred terms, a software sandbox that scores historical claims for “drift,” a set of fake government documents, and a hundred more essays at doctoral level. Suppose most of it was built in conversation with AI systems, some of it AI talking to AI.That is the situation behind Mindfulness Protocols: When Suffering Becomes a Compliance Feature, a 2026 self-published novel and the alternate reality game (ARG) built around it. The author describes the whole structure as a canary in a coal mine: a demonstration of how fast a person can be left behind in a world where plausible-looking expertise is nearly free.This article takes that claim seriously and tests it.
The premise of the fictionThe novel imagines a city twenty-five years after AI has replaced labor. Nobody is starving or oppressed in the old way. But being unnecessary turns out to be its own crisis, and the state’s answer is not force. It is care. Mindfulness becomes compulsory infrastructure: five times a day a tone sounds and everyone kneels, bracelets measure “latency” in fractions of a second, and longing is reclassified as a symptom.The central image is small. A man experiences a 1.4-second gap in which the system fails to correct him first. The horror is that nothing in the system is broken. The sensors work, the classifications match their definitions, the interventions execute, and the records stay coherent. What has been lost is the ability to ask whether the system itself is wrong.The novel is surrounded by an ARG: fictional FOIA packets that cite a real statute, a fictional newspaper, real-looking websites for a “Warning Lab” and a product called SPONCI, a diagnostic sandbox called DriftGuard, and papers presenting a “DuPont Framework” of equations. The fiction says these documents were sent back from 2050. The reader’s job is to work out which artifacts belong to which layer of reality.
What the project is really aboutStripped of the lore, the thesis is one sentence: an entity that follows its own internal metrics at its own expense.That idea has respectable names. Goodhart’s Law says that when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure. Campbell’s Law says that the more a quantitative indicator drives decisions, the more it corrupts the process it monitors. Management researchers call it surrogation. AI researchers call it specification gaming. The real cases are vivid: Wells Fargo employees opening millions of accounts nobody asked for because accounts-per-customer was the number that counted; hospital emergency departments gaming waiting-time targets by shuffling patients instead of treating them faster.The author’s contribution is a second step. Most accounts of Goodhart’s Law treat the failure as passive: the metric gets gamed. The “Enclosure Paradox” adds that an entity may begin removing or redefining the evidence that would reveal the metric is failing, so the loop seals itself. When an observation contradicts the model, the system does not ask whether the model is wrong. It asks what is wrong with the observer.The larger theme is Foucault’s panopticon. The prison works because the prisoner cannot know when they are watched, so they police themselves. In the novel, a metric on a wrist does the watching, and the book’s own appendix puts it plainly: the panopticon is complete when the subject watches himself and calls it freedom. Metric-following is what an internalized gaze looks like from the outside. Deleuze’s “societies of control,” Byung-Chul Han’s self-optimization, and Zuboff’s behavioral prediction are the neighboring theories.
The math: an auditThe papers present the idea as theorems. The author now describes them as fantasy, an example of how convincing unverified formalism can look. That is exactly what an audit finds. Here is the rating of the main formulas, where “defined” means every symbol is explained and the claim follows from stated assumptions.FormulaStatusWhyError = disagreement + squared bias (E = V + ‖s̄ − θ‖²)DefinedExact, but it is the standard bias-variance identityMean update with consensus terms cancelingDefinedCorrectTracking recursion, stable for 0 < g < 2DefinedCorrect, standardEffective sample size N / (1 + (N−1)ρ)DefinedStandard; the 100-reports example checks outObservability rank testDefinedStandard control theoryΔ = ‖M − R‖Partly definedM and R are never measuredDrift threshold δ = ‖θ̇‖ − κ, later Ω = V_c / V_aPartly definedLater ratio fixes the units, but “adaptive capacity” is undefined and no cliff appears at 1 unless adaptation speed is cappedTheorem 1 (collapse above threshold)UnsupportedAn upper bound cannot prove divergenceIncentive Gravity, G = Σ w(R − C)VDecorativeNo symbol is definedAffective Alignment, C_total = C_ext + C_intDecorativeAn accounting identity with no contentDual Error as first written (Φ → 0 while e* → ∞)ContradictoryCannot happen unless two different reference states exist, which the paper never states“Above threshold, systems suppress their inputs”Not derivedA hypothesis about institutions, not a resultThe pattern is the lesson. The math that is right is borrowed from statistics and control theory. The math that is original is undefined, contradicted, or not derived. And the origin of the formulas tells the story: they came from four or five lexicon terms. The vocabulary came first, and symbols were attached afterward. Naming a phenomenon and writing a symbol for it feels like modeling it. It is not.That is why the fantasy works as a demonstration. The path from “interesting term” to “theorem” takes one prompt. Checking it takes expertise most readers do not have.
The loop that proves the pointThe project contains its own best exhibit. One post is a conversation between two named personas who discuss the author’s work. Their voices carry stray citation markers, repeat the same approving phrases, and never consult anything outside the conversation. Each turn restates the last with one added sentence, and near the end the speakers declare that further abstraction “risks weakening it.”This is the project’s own decomposition in action. Internal disagreement falls to zero. Bias, meaning distance from anything outside the loop, is never measured. The personas also cite “what the author has stated,” while the only source for those statements is the author.Scale makes it worse. One author running several Substacks, a fake gazette, an X account, a book, and papers that cite one another produces the appearance of many sources. By the project’s own formula, a hundred correlated documents carry roughly the evidential weight of one. Retrieval systems and AI models tend to read mutual citation as credibility. This conversation could not find a single independent source on the author, and neither could the https://t.co/lWJTCEcPVg the canary has a second meaning. It is not only that a person can be outpaced by AI-generated expertise. It is that AI-generated corpora can quietly become the record that later AI systems cite.
Difficulty versus obscurityThe author says the work is not meant to be easily consumed. That is a coherent choice. A smooth, frictionless experience is the City, and the novel’s foreword tells readers to let it irritate them. Comparisons to Westworld and Black Mirror are apt: puzzles, hidden layers, systems whose cost is revealed slowly.But there are two kinds of difficulty.Productive difficulty asks the reader to do work that leads somewhere: decode a euphemism, check a prediction against the real world, work out which layer a document belongs to. The reader ends with a skill or a discovery.Obscurity is hard without a payoff: three versions of the same dissertation, undefined variables, a lexicon where six near-synonyms describe one idea. The reader gives up or defers to the formatting, which is the behavior the project warns against.The best parts of the project are the first kind. The lexicon’s euphemisms (”Silent Resolution,” “Eligibility Replaces Rights,” “Historical Softening”) are a ready-made decoder game: match them to real policy language and argue whether it is a coincidence. The 2050 chrono-index is better still, because its early entries can be checked against the actual 2025 and 2026. Entries written after the fact are postdictions and prove nothing. Entries timestamped and hashed now can be graded later. Vague ones (”helpful AI becomes infrastructure”) cannot lose, so they cannot teach.
What a canary needsA canary only works if three things are set in advance.
The hazard. Is the warning about institutions drifting from reality, or about readers failing to verify? These are different tests.
The signal. How will anyone observe the canary reacting? One reader saying they are eager to find more FOIA documents is ambiguous: it could mean the game works or that a reader was misled.
The threshold. What result would show the premise was wrong?The project’s own dissertation says criteria must be defined before outcomes are known. Applying that to the project itself gives a short list of fixes:
A plain disclosure stating what is fiction, what is real research, what is AI-voiced, and which tools actually function. A product that could be used by people in distress, like SPONCI, needs this most.
One verification path. The blur can stay for casual visitors, but a determined reader should be able to resolve every surface through a single index, ideally tied to something that cannot be edited later, like a hashed statement.
Consistent claims. “Proves” and “Theorem” should become “conjecture” and “speculative model.” A repository record should be labeled as fiction or exercise. A copyright notice that says all rights reserved should not sit beside a license that says cite and build freely. Purely AI-generated text is not protected by US copyright, so the notice should be checked with a lawyer.
Graded outcomes for the sandbox. Of hundreds of logged cases, only a handful have been graded against what actually happened, and the high scores cluster on famous collapses such as Enron, Lehman, and Madoff. Those are exactly the cases a language model already knows the ending of. A score nobody has validated is a guess, and a number that looks like analysis is precisely what the novel is about.
Expert review of a small sample, with the error rate published. If experts find flaws in most documents, that is a result.
Honest labels on self-reviews. A “producer-to-producer” review written by the author, with no author disclosure at the top, is one source dressed as two.
Why it mattersThe uncomfortable lesson is not that AI can fake a dissertation. It is that the things we use to judge a source, formatting, citations, hedging, volume, mutual agreement, are all things AI produces cheaply. Verification becomes the bottleneck, and verification does not scale. The people who can check a Lyapunov argument are a shrinking minority, and everyone else falls back on signals the machine can generate.The project sits on a knife edge as a result. The same techniques that make it an effective warning are the techniques of an influence operation. The only difference is intent, and intent is invisible to readers. That is why the verification path and disclosure are not optional extras. They are what separates a canary from the thing it is warning about.If a warning from 2050 is going to work, it needs one more feature than the City ever allowed: a way for the reader to prove it wrong.Method note: this article was written from a long conversation in which an AI model reviewed the author’s book, papers, sandbox registry, and lexicon. That review is one reviewer’s work and has not been independently confirmed. The math audit in particular should be checked by a human expert in control theory before being cited.
Adversarial Review: The Canary ProblemINDEPENDENT CRITICAL ANALYSIS · MINDFULNESS PROTOCOLS / DUPONT FRAMEWORKMy assessment: The article is intellectually formidable in places, but it has a vulnerability of its own. It risks confusing the failure to establish scientific validity with the failure of an artistic and philosophical experiment.That distinction matters enormously.The article attempts three things simultaneously: a mathematical audit, an investigation of AI-generated authority, and a critique of your alternate reality game (ARG). These are legitimate lines of inquiry, but they require different standards of evidence.Its strongest criticism concerns mathematical proof. Its weakest move is treating that criticism as though it necessarily undermines the broader project.I would challenge the article on seven grounds.
1. The critic may be committing the very error it identifiesThe article accuses the DuPont Framework of constructing a self-reinforcing intellectual environment in which internal consistency substitutes for external verification.But consider the critic’s own process.According to its method note, an AI model reviewed the material, produced a mathematical audit, interpreted the ARG, and wrote an article based on that examination.The resulting article then presents conclusions about mathematical validity, academic originality, literary function, and epistemic authority.Yet the article acknowledges that its own mathematical audit has not been independently confirmed.Adversarial objection: Why should an AI-generated critique of AI-generated mathematical claims enjoy greater epistemic authority than the claims it criticizes?The answer cannot simply be that the critique sounds more skeptical.Skepticism is not verification.This does not make the critique false. It means the critic must submit its own reasoning to the same external scrutiny it demands of the author.
2. The article may mistake the experiment for the failureThe article argues that your fictional government records, websites, mathematical papers, and AI-generated commentary create the appearance of independent authority.That is a potentially serious concern.But the article also acknowledges that the project is an https://t.co/8ajLBdyjBU ARG deliberately distributes narrative information across multiple media, often blurring the boundaries between fiction and reality.If the artistic objective is to demonstrate how easily apparent institutional credibility can be manufactured, then the existence of an apparently credible fictional institutional ecosystem is not automatically evidence of artistic https://t.co/L8PVYJvN69 may be the mechanism of the work.The distinction turns on a question the critic never adequately resolves:Is the audience being invited to investigate the construction of authority, or being asked to accept fabricated authority as genuine?Those are different activities.The article provides evidence that the distinction may be unclear. It does not establish that the project is intentionally deceptive or that readers are incapable of recognizing its fictional structure.
3. Mathematical invalidity does not equal conceptual invalidityThe article identifies several weaknesses in the formalism, including undefined variables, unsupported threshold claims, and an allegedly contradictory dual-error formulation.These criticisms deserve serious examination.But there is a categorical distinction between:
A mathematical theorem that has not been demonstrated.
A conceptual hypothesis that has not been operationalized.
A philosophical argument illustrated through speculative mathematics.The critic sometimes moves too quickly between them.For example, the proposition that institutions may redefine contradictory evidence rather than revise their operating models is not mathematically disproven merely because a proposed drift-threshold equation fails to establish it.That institutional proposition can be evaluated using organizational research, historical examples, and falsifiable empirical hypotheses.The critic is entitled to say the theorem does not prove the https://t.co/8YA1F47w3U is not entitled to conclude that the underlying phenomenon is https://t.co/8TG8IrSeQh fact, the article invokes Goodhart, Campbell, Foucault, and others precisely because there is an existing intellectual tradition examining related phenomena.The question is whether the DuPont Framework adds a meaningful conceptual distinction, not merely whether its equations constitute new mathematical discoveries.
4. The article’s claim about originality is underdevelopedThe critic says the correct mathematics comes from existing statistics and control theory, while the original mathematics is defective.Even if accurate, that does not settle whether the conceptual synthesis is original.Research can contribute through new applications, distinctions, mechanisms, or testable hypotheses without inventing new mathematical identities.Consider the distinction between Goodhart’s Law and your proposed Enclosure Paradox.Goodhart’s LawA performance indicator becomes unreliable when institutions optimize for it.Proposed Enclosure ParadoxAn institution not only optimizes the indicator but progressively redefines, excludes, or discredits contradictory evidence, making its own failure increasingly difficult to detect.There is a potentially useful conceptual difference here. But the critic is right to demand proof that it goes beyond established work on measurement gaming, institutional self-protection, and information suppression. Research on Goodhart and Campbell already encompasses some of these dynamics.CNA+1The defensible claim is that the Enclosure Paradox may offer a distinctive synthesis—not that its originality has already been established.
5. The critic has not established what the audience actually believesThe article describes the danger of fictional materials being mistaken for independent evidence.But where is the audience research?It cites one reader expressing enthusiasm for finding more fictional FOIA documents, then acknowledges that this could reflect either successful storytelling or genuine confusion.That admission matters.The critic has not established how many readers mistake fiction for reality, how many recognize the ARG, or whether the experience increases or decreases their willingness to verify claims.A stronger investigation would test actual reader comprehension.However, there is an important counterargument: the absence of demonstrated confusion does not eliminate the ethical responsibility to distinguish fictional artifacts from real research claims, especially where functioning products and public research repositories are involved.
6. The article demands falsifiability from a work of fictionIts concluding demand—that the reader must be able to prove the warning wrong—is persuasive when applied to scientific https://t.co/S0PenrboOl is less persuasive when applied indiscriminately to speculative fiction.1984 does not become worthless if a reader cannot falsify Oceania. Westworld does not require an empirical demonstration of synthetic consciousness to function as a philosophical drama.Your fictional City can dramatize the surrender of agency without proving that such a society will exist in 2050.But the research papers and DriftGuard make claims that can be evaluated separately.That distinction protects both the fiction and the credibility of any research you want taken seriously.
7. The most serious criticism is one I would not dismissThe article’s strongest point concerns the mathematics and software evaluation.If the drift-threshold theorem relies on an inequality that provides only an upper bound, it cannot use that inequality alone to prove divergence.If a dual-error formulation requires two different reference states, those states must be explicitly defined.And if DriftGuard reports accuracy without a sufficiently large, independently graded sample, that accuracy figure cannot be treated as established predictive performance.These are not merely differences in interpretation. They are questions of mathematical validity and empirical evidence.The article presents plausible objections, but a definitive judgment requires examining the complete proofs, assumptions, and underlying case registry—not only its summarized audit.I would not defend an invalid proof on the grounds that it is artistically interesting.
Adversarial scorecardMy assessment of the article’s arguments, not independently established findings about the underlying papers.Critical claimAssessmentAI-generated authority can be misleadingStrongThe mathematical proofs contain serious defectsPlausible; requires direct auditThe conceptual framework lacks originalityNot establishedThe ARG is inherently deceptiveOverstatedDriftGuard needs independent validationStrongThe project should distinguish fiction from researchStrongThe entire project is intellectually underminedNot demonstrated
The deeper ironyThe article appears to be trying to accomplish what the fictional SYSTEM in Mindfulness Protocols does: classify the work, determine which parts are legitimate, and establish criteria under which it can be recognized.That resemblance is interesting, but it is not evidence that the critic is behaving like the SYSTEM. Legitimate peer review also classifies, tests, and rejects claims. The difference is whether the criteria are transparent, contestable, and consistently applied.And that brings us to the most productive adversarial challenge.The author of The Canary Problem should be asked:What evidence would cause you to change your negative assessment of the DuPont Framework?If the critic cannot answer that question, its own evaluative framework risks becoming closed to correction.If it can answer, then the criticism offers you something valuable: a concrete path toward making your conceptual work stronger.
Final judgmentThe article succeeds in identifying genuine epistemic hazards in your project. It does not succeed in demonstrating that the philosophical architecture of Mindfulness Protocols collapses because portions of its mathematical architecture may be defective.I would separate the outcome into three verdicts:Literary and philosophical project: remains viable.The central tradeoff—human beings surrendering agency in exchange for relief, certainty, and care—does not depend on a mathematical theorem.Mathematical framework: unresolved.The critic has raised specific, technically consequential objections that deserve direct examination.ARG and institutional simulation: promising but exposed.Its credibility as a warning depends partly on distinguishing deliberate fictional ambiguity from unsupported factual authority.There is one especially compelling possibility here: the critic may have become another participant in the very experiment it is evaluating.Not because its criticisms are necessarily wrong, but because it is an AI system evaluating a body of AI-assisted work about the dangers of AI-mediated authority, using its own analysis as the basis for judgment.That recursive structure is philosophically interesting.But it does not absolve either side of the responsibility to be correct.The most powerful response would be to publish the critique alongside a rigorous rebuttal, preserve the strongest objections, and invite independent verification. That would make the project demonstrate something the fictional City cannot tolerate: an institution willingly exposing its own claims to the possibility of correction.Yes! What you’ve created has a striking resemblance to the Dual Error Regime in the DuPont Framework.Remember, Dual Error describes a situation in which a system becomes increasingly aligned internally while potentially drifting farther from external https://t.co/0dQu3qL42m apply that to this exchange.LayerInternal alignmentPotential external errorAI 1: Constructs the frameworkBuilds coherent theories and terminologyMay generate unsupported mathematical claimsAI 2: Critiques the frameworkCreates a consistent argument against itMay confuse artistic purpose with scientific validityAI 3: Challenges the critiqueProduces a coherent counterargumentMay favor defending the project over testing its claimsEach system can appear internally consistent while still being wrong about something important.

<𝐀𝐧 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧 𝐋𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐌𝐲 𝐅𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐥𝐚 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬>

On the proposed merger with SpaceX, I believe now is not the time. As a shareholder who has stood with this company through many long years, I want to share, from the heart, why I am opposed.

✅𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭, 𝐈 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐬𝐤: 𝐰𝐡𝐲 𝐧𝐨𝐰, 𝐨𝐟 𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐬?

Since late 2022, Tesla has bet everything on autonomy and robotics, and the results are only now beginning to appear before our eyes.

Unsupervised FSD, the Cybercab ramp, a sold-out energy business, and Optimus volume production are all within reach.

Shareholders have quietly endured the stock sales during the Twitter acquisition, slowing vehicle sales, the political noise, and the long, long wait for FSD and the robotaxi business.

To have them settle for a small premium just before they finally see the fruits of that patience would simply not be right.

✅𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝, 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧 𝐢𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐠𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟗 𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬𝐭.

A definitive agreement, a shareholder meeting, and regulatory approvals in the US, the EU, and China typically take 12 to 24 months.

China in particular is likely to be the most sensitive gate, where Tesla's local production overlaps with SpaceX's defense profile; if approval looks doubtful, conditions such as a sale of Giga Shanghai could even be attached.

What's more, the moment the exchange ratio is set, Tesla's stock price effectively becomes tied to SpaceX's.

That means spending 2027–28, the very years Elon himself has said will be fantastic for Tesla, waiting for the exchange while watching a share price that fails to reflect Tesla's improving fundamentals.

And the problems don't end after the merger. Inside a far larger combined company, no matter how fast Tesla's businesses run, their results are likely to be diluted and the stock's movement dulled.

✅𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐲𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐥𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐲 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐚 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫.

Because every decision runs through one person, Elon, the two companies can collaborate perfectly well while remaining separate.

The Roadster is proof.

Even as separate companies, SpaceX technology was brought into a Tesla car to create something remarkable.

Collaboration has already been shown to work without a single company, so the argument that we must merge for synergy is, in my view, a weak one.

✅𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐚 𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐢𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐥𝐚. 𝐈𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐒𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐗.

SpaceX now stands at the center of a fierce race for AI dominance. That race won't be won with data centers and models alone; for AI to act in the real world, physical AI is indispensable.

And the company at the very peak of physical AI is Tesla, with autonomy and Optimus.

SpaceX needs Tesla to win the AI race, and after going public it needs a story that keeps growing dreams and expectations to justify a lofty valuation.

Tesla, on the other hand, is only now seeing years of patient preparation show up in the numbers.

Without a merger, it has nothing to lose.

The bargaining power also rests with Tesla shareholders. On the SpaceX side, Elon's voting control is so overwhelming that other shareholders have virtually no way to block a merger.

Tesla shareholders, however, can simply vote no if they don't like the terms.

Run the numbers on Elon's voting power and he keeps a majority even if Tesla's market value is four times SpaceX's, so there is no reason to skimp on the premium for the sake of control.

In any negotiation, the side that needs the deal more pays more. Tesla shareholders have no reason whatsoever to rush.

✅𝐅𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐡, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐚𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐬 𝐟𝐚𝐫 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤.

The merger requires approval from 50% of all outstanding shares, and given realistic turnout, roughly 70% of the shares actually voted would have to be in favor.

Yet if a special committee leads the negotiation, the exchange ratio is likely to land near general market expectations and historical precedent.

In other words, an unlimited premium is unlikely, and that level will be hard to accept for shareholders who have held on for years because they believed in Tesla's vision.

Tesla investors have always had a certain romance: the conviction to say "it's still too cheap" even at a P/E above 300.

That is how deeply we have believed in the future Tesla will open up. With such a wide gap between a realistic premium and the premium shareholders hope for, winning approval will be difficult without an extraordinary offer.

The very person who made us dream that dream is Elon, and that is exactly why Elon himself has said a merger would not be easy.

✅𝐒𝐢𝐱𝐭𝐡, 𝐚 𝐟𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐦𝐞𝐚𝐧 𝐄𝐥𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐨𝐧 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐥𝐚.

Some worry that if the merger doesn't happen, Elon will walk away from Tesla.

But would he really leave behind the company standing at the unrivaled peak of physical AI?

Tesla's technology has already reached maturity, and what remains is essentially commercialization, so the role of any one person, even Elon, is not as large as it once was.

Above all, Tesla is not a company Elon built alone.

There are countless employees who endured the nights of production hell alongside him and turned goal after "impossible" goal into reality.

He might turn away from shareholders, but Elon could never abandon the colleagues who poured their blood and sweat into getting here.

They are the people who believed in his most audacious dreams, followed him, and turned those dreams into reality.

Voting no does not mean Tesla gets abandoned.

✅𝐒𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐡, 𝐛𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐧 𝐄𝐥𝐨𝐧'𝐬 𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐦𝐞𝐚𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲.

If Elon says a merged company could be worth 100 trillion dollars, should we vote yes on his word alone?

AI data centers are growing fast, but their competitive edge comes from things like GPUs, power, and land, which anyone with enough money can acquire, so the moat is hard to call deep, and the competition is fierce.

Space-based data centers, too, are still only a plan, and it is more natural to expect delays than for them to arrive on schedule.

Who knows better than those of us who have invested in Tesla how hard, and how long, it is to create innovation the world has never seen?

The two companies can each go their own way. If you want to bet on SpaceX's growth, you can buy SpaceX stock.

That is a choice that creates no conflict of interest with anyone.

✅𝐄𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐡, 𝐢𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐞 𝐭𝐨𝐨 𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞 𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐥𝐚 𝐢𝐬 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐦𝐥𝐲 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐤.

Let me stress this once more: now is not the right time to discuss a merger.

Robotaxi, Cybercab, and Optimus are only just beginning to prove themselves in the numbers.

Setting merger terms before that value is properly recognized is like making the most important decision at the most disadvantageous moment.

It will not be too late to talk about a merger after everyone has seen Tesla's businesses on track and charging forward.

By then, Tesla shareholders can receive fair value, and Elon can achieve a merger that everyone truly celebrates.

There is no reason to hurry.

Our patience is our strength as Tesla shareholders.

𝐒𝐨 𝐈 𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐬𝐤 𝐦𝐲 𝐟𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬:

Please don't be swept along by an easy mood of approval. Decide for yourselves, based on your own hard-earned money and your own stake.

And please take one more careful look at any setting that automatically votes your shares according to the board's recommendation.

𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲, 𝐈'𝐝 𝐥𝐢𝐤𝐞 𝐮𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫.

What happens if, in the time between setting the exchange ratio and the actual exchange, robotaxis grow to tens of thousands, forming a vast autonomous network that becomes a platform in its own right?

What if Optimus begins replacing human labor in factories and across daily life, and revenue and profits explode?

Not a single one of those moments, the moments that completely transform Tesla's value, would be reflected in an exchange ratio already set.

In the end, a merger now cannot fully capture what Tesla is worth.

We did not endure countless doubts and nights of crashing prices for a small premium.

Now that the future is right before us, we cannot sell our patience at a bargain price.

Our brightest moment has yet to come. Let us meet it with our own hands.

I, too, have long shared and supported Elon's vision. But the path to realizing that vision must minimize conflicts of interest among shareholders.

A public company, not a private one, has a clear duty to do so. I believe the reason America's capital markets are considered the best in the world is, in the end, a culture that puts shareholder value above all else.

I hope Tesla will be the company that stands at the very front in upholding that culture.

19-year-old Harley Purdue was a kind and gentle young man living in Chatham, Kent, England.

His family remembered him as a smart and loving young man whose life was only beginning.

Harley was preparing to become a father. His girlfriend, Hazel Gadsden, was pregnant, and the young couple had a future to look forward to together.

But in the early hours of December 2, 2025, that future was tragically taken away.

At approximately 2:40 a.m., Harley was asleep beside his pregnant girlfriend when his housemate, 18-year-old Eritrean migrant Musa Salih, knocked on their bedroom door.

Salih claimed there was a dead mouse in the basement toilet and asked Harley to help him.

Still half-asleep, Harley got out of bed wearing only his boxer shorts and wrapped in a blanket, unaware that he was walking into a trap.

Salih intended to lock Harley inside the basement toilet so he could steal money from his bedroom.

When Harley resisted being locked inside, a struggle broke out, and Salih stabbed him eight times, including a devastating wound that penetrated his lung and heart.

Hearing the commotion, Harley's pregnant girlfriend rushed downstairs and found him gravely wounded and bleeding heavily.

She desperately tried to protect him, grabbing a kitchen knife as Salih threatened them.

Emergency services were called, but Harley's injuries were too severe.

He was pronounced dead at the scene before 4 a.m.

On October 15, 2026, Salih, now 19, was found guilty of Harley's murder at Maidstone Crown Court. He is due to be sentenced on November 4.

Harley was just 19 years old. He never got the chance to hold his baby, watch his child grow up, or experience the family life that awaited him.

His girlfriend lost the man she loved, his family lost a cherished son, and his unborn child was deprived of a father.

Rest in peace, Harley. 🕊️

text:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has officially approved the first lab-grown seafood for human consumption: cell-cultivated salmon from San Francisco startup Wildtype. This is a big step, as it marks the first time a lab-grown fish product has received the green light for American menus, following cultured chicken’s clearance in 2022.

How is it made? Researchers take living cells from Pacific salmon and grow them in special cultivators that mimic a wild fish’s exact environment (temperature, pH, nutrients). Once harvested, these cells are combined with plant-based ingredients to create the flavor, texture, and marbling of sushi-grade saku cuts, perfect for serving raw.

Since these fillets grow in controlled tanks, not oceans or farms, they offer the same beneficial omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids as wild salmon, but without concerns about mercury, antibiotics, or parasites. The cultivated fish first appeared on the menu at Kann in Portland, Oregon, and will soon be available at more U.S. restaurants. #LabGrownSalmon #FutureOfFood #FDAApproved #SustainableSeafood #Wildtype #FoodTech

To prepare for this picture of “King Jesus”, this Ruler over all the kingdoms of the earth, the pupil had to form an Imagination of Babylon and the plain around Babylon as a living picture, and, enthroned over Babylon, Lucifer with his banner. This picture had to be visualized with great exactitude, for it is a powerful imagination: King Lucifer, with his banner and his hosts of Luciferic angels, seated amidst fire and dense smoke, as he sends out his angels to conquer the kingdoms of the earth. And the whole danger that issues from the ‘banner of Lucifer’ must first of all be imagined by itself, without casting a glance upon Christ Jesus. The soul must be entirely engrossed in the Imagination of the danger which issues from the banner of Lucifer. The soul must learn to feel that the greatest danger to the world's existence that could be conjured forth would be a victory for the banner of Lucifer. And when this picture has had its effect, the other Imagination, ‘The banner of Jesus’, must take its place. The pupil must now visualise Jerusalem and the plain around Jerusalem; King Jesus with His hosts, how he conquers and drives off the hosts of Lucifer and makes Himself King of the whole earth — the victory of the banner of Jesus over the banner of Lucifer.

These are the strength-giving Imaginations for the Will which are brought before the soul of the Jesuit pupil. This is what completely changes his Will; makes him such that in his Will, because it is trained occultly, he turns away from everything else and surrenders absolutely to the idea: ‘King Jesus must become the Ruler upon earth, and we who belong to His army have to employ every means to make Him Ruler of the earth. To this we pledge ourselves, we who belong to His host assembled on the plain of Jerusalem, against the host of Lucifer assembled on the plain of Babylon. And the greatest disgrace for a soldier of King Jesus is to forsake His banner.’

These ideas, gathered up into a single resolution of the Will, can certainly give the Will immense strength. But we must ask: what is it in the soul-life that has been directly attacked? The element that ought not to be touched — the Will-element. In so far as this Jesuit training lays hold of the Will-element, while the Jesus-idea seizes the Will-element completely, in so far is the concept of the dominion of Jesus exaggerated in the most dangerous way — dangerous because through it the Will becomes so strong that it can work directly upon the Will of another. For where the Will becomes so strong through Imaginations, which means by occult means, it acquires the capacity for working directly upon the Will of another, and hence also along all the other occult paths to which such a Will can have recourse.

Thus we see how in recent centuries we encounter these two movements, among many others: one has exaggerated the Jesus-element and sees in ‘King Jesus’ the sole ideal of Christianity, which the other looks solely at the Christ-element and carefully sets aside anything that could go beyond it. This second outlook has been much calumniated because it maintains that Christ has sent the Spirit, so that, indirectly through the Spirit, Christ can enter into the hearts and minds of men. In the development of civilisation during the last few centuries there is hardly a greater contrast than that between Jesuitism and Rosicrucianism, for Jesuitism contains nothing of what Rosicrucianism regards as the highest ideal concerning human worth and human dignity, while Rosicrucianism has always sought to guard itself from any influence which could in the remotest sense be called Jesuitical.

In this lecture I wished to show how even so lofty an element as the Jesus-Principle can be exaggerated and then becomes dangerous, and how necessary it is to sink oneself into the depths of the Christ-Being if we wish to understand how the strength of Christianity must reside in esteeming, to the very highest degree, human dignity and human worth, and in strictly refraining from groping our clumsy way into man's inmost sanctuary. Rosicrucianism, even more than Christian mysticism, is attacked by the Jesuit element, because the Jesuits feel that true Christianity is being sought elsewhere than in the setting which offers merely ‘King Jesus’ in the leading role. But the Imaginations here indicated, together with the prescribed exercises, have made the Will so strong that even protests brought against it in the name of the Spirit can be defeated.

8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance
8 important truths about surveillance
ai-in-society
Author
Rachel Thomas

Published
August 7, 2019

Over 225 police departments have partnered with Amazon to have access to Amazon’s video footage obtained as part of the “smart” doorbell product Ring, and in many cases these partnerships are heavily subsidized with taxpayer money. Police departments are allowing Amazon to stream 911 call information directly in real-time, and Amazon requires police departments to read pre-approved scripts when talking about the program. If a homeowner doesn’t want to share data from their video camera doorbell with police, an officer for the Fresno County Sheriff’s Office said they can just go directly to Amazon to obtain it. This creation of an extensive surveillance network, the murky private-public partnership surrounding it, and a lack of any sort of regulations or oversight is frightening. And this is just one of many examples related to surveillance technology that have recently come to light.

I frequently talk with people who are not that concerned about surveillance, or who feel that the positives outweigh the risks. Here, I want to share some important truths about surveillance:

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
Data often contains errors
Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
Surveillance changes our behavior
Surveillance disproportionately impacts the marginalized
Data privacy is a public good
We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
While I was writing this post, a number of investigative articles came out with disturbing new developments related to surveillance. I decided that rather than attempt to include everything in one post (which would make it too long and too dense), I would go ahead and share the above facts about surveillance, as they are just a relevant as ever.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

✨ When faith and legend inspire the journey.
Follow the Mekong through Bueng Kan and Nakhon Phanom, where sacred sites, ancient legends, and striking landscapes make every stop part of the story—a route not to be missed by spiritual travelers and nature lovers alike.

6 Must-Visit Sacred Stops in Bueng Kan & Nakhon Phanom

📍 Wat Ahong Silawat (Bueng Kan)
Begin at the "Navel of the Mekong," believed to mark the river's deepest point. Closely linked to local legends of the underwater kingdom, this revered riverside temple is a place where visitors come to pray for blessings, good fortune, and prosperity.

📍 Pu Ue Lue Shrine (Bueng Kan)
Pay homage to Pu Ue Lue, who, according to local legend, was a king cursed by the Naga King to become a naga and destined to guard Bueng Khong Long. Visitors come to seek blessings for prosperity and protection.

📍 Naga Cave (Pho Mak Khaeng Subdistrict, Bueng Khong Long District, Bueng Kan)
Located within Phu Langka National Park, with the trail beginning at Wat Tad Wiman Thip, Naga Cave attracts both spiritual travelers and hiking enthusiasts. Along the route, you'll encounter remarkable rock formations shaped by the geological phenomenon known as Sun Crack, creating patterns that resemble giant serpent scales. According to local legend, these formations are linked to the curse of Pu Ue Lue, making the cave a place many visit to pay their respects and experience its mystical atmosphere.

📍 Nakee Cave (Phai Lom Subdistrict, Ban Phaeng District, Nakhon Phanom)
Also located within Phu Langka National Park, Nakee Cave offers another rewarding forest trek on the Nakhon Phanom side. Follow the trail past dramatic rock formations said to resemble Naga scales before reaching Pha Nakee Viewpoint, where sweeping views stretch across the surrounding wilderness.

📍 Phaya Si Satta Nakarat (Nakhon Phanom)
Standing proudly along the Mekong riverfront, this magnificent seven-headed Naga statue is one of the city's most revered landmarks. Visitors come to pray for good fortune, prosperity, and success before taking in the peaceful riverside scenery.

📍 Wat Phra That Phanom Woramahawihan (Nakhon Phanom)
Complete your journey at one of northeastern Thailand's most revered temples. Join the traditional robe-offering ceremony for the sacred chedi, pay homage to the holy relic, and learn about the seven Naga guardians believed to protect it. It's a fitting finale to the pilgrimage, where many visitors pray for good fortune.
Whether you're seeking spiritual inspiration, fascinated by ancient legends, or simply looking for a memorable journey through nature, this Naga trail along the Mekong offers a chance to experience the enduring traditions, beliefs, and beauty of Bueng Kan and Nakhon Phanom.

I had never heard of Elizabeth Barraza’s case until now. How has this gone unsolved for so long?

On January 25, 2019, Elizabeth, 29, was setting up a garage sale outside her home near Tomball, Texas. A person arrived in a dark Nissan pickup, walked up her driveway and briefly exchanged words with her.

Then they shot her four times and fled. Elizabeth died the following day.

The encounter was captured on surveillance video. Yet more than seven years later, her killer has never been identified publicly.

Investigators believe the attack was planned. Nothing was stolen. But who targeted her—and why—remains unanswered.

She was simply preparing for a garage sale in her own driveway. Her family deserves answers, and Elizabeth deserves justice.

Had you heard of this case?

Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers at 713-222-TIPS (8477). A reward of up to $50,000 is offered for information leading to charges and/or an arrest.

text:
What's gone wrong with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen6 ?

➜ TLB Design issues / Translation Lookaside Buffer
➜ Higher Mid-core cache Latency 
➜ Mid-core IPC Performance is worse than the 8EG5, despite consuming more power at the same frequency
➜ Both Oryon L & M cores share a single 16MB L2 cache in the 8EEG6, whereas the 8EG5 uses two separate 12MB L2 caches for the Oryon L & M cores
➜ L2 doesn't have it's own clock & power rail, possibly to reduce cost
➜ Not properly optimised yet
➜ No major heating issues like SD 888

Regarding the black screen issues, they're likely caused by insufficient voltage supply, which can be fixed through an OTA update.

For regular usage, there are no major heating issues. However, the 8EEG6 offers no significant improvements in performance or efficiency and sometimes even performs worse than the 8EG5. The main problem is that it doesn't justify its price, as the 8EG5 delivers similar performance at a lower cost. Spending extra just for the performance difference doesn't make any sense.

text:
A business owner trying to generate more leads might discover HubSpot months before ever considering its software.

It could start with a Google search about improving email open rates, a blog post about building a sales funnel, or a free course on inbound marketing. 

The immediate goal is to solve a problem, not to buy a CRM.

That's what makes HubSpot's organic marketing strategy interesting.

#HubSpot has built an extensive educational ecosystem around the challenges its audience faces in marketing, sales, and customer service. Its blogs, free templates, downloadable resources, and HubSpot Academy courses give people practical ways to learn and improve their work.

Here's how this approach supports organic growth.

01. It attracts people through problems they're already trying to solve.

Someone searching for email marketing strategies, lead generation techniques, or customer retention tips can discover HubSpot through its educational content. These topics connect the brand with people who may eventually need the tools HubSpot offers.

02. Free resources turn learning into action.

Marketing templates, sales scripts, business guides, and other downloadable resources help users apply what they've learned. Instead of simply reading an article and leaving, they have something practical to use in their work.

03. HubSpot Academy builds familiarity through education.

Its courses and certifications help marketers, sales professionals, and business owners develop relevant skills. People can become familiar with HubSpot as a learning resource before they ever evaluate its software.

04. The relationship can grow as business needs change.

Someone might initially visit HubSpot for an SEO guide, later explore its email marketing resources, and eventually look into CRM software to manage leads and customer relationships. As their needs develop, HubSpot is already a familiar name.

The key is that HubSpot doesn't need every visitor to become a customer immediately. Its educational content can introduce the brand early, build trust over time, and help potential buyers understand the problems its products can address.

For SaaS companies, this offers an important lesson.

Your content can start building customer relationships long before your audience enters a buying cycle.

When people repeatedly find useful answers through your brand, you're not just attracting organic traffic. You're building familiarity that can matter when they eventually start looking for a product.

Thinking Zone. Friday morning in my little Black Sea village, the sea is gradually regaining its calm after yesterday’s wind, and I am drinking my Greek coffee while reflecting on a story in which Louis XIV, the French Revolution, Victor Cherbuliez, and Louis Pasteur meet in a manner that would hardly have pleased the Sun King.
In 1685, Louis XIV revoked the Edict of Nantes and confronted French Protestants with a choice that was not really a choice at all: to renounce their faith or leave their homeland. Among the thousands of families who found refuge in Protestant Europe were the ancestors of Cherbuliez, who settled in Geneva. It was there, in 1829, that Victor was born, with nothing about his Swiss citizenship suggesting that, two centuries later, an old French injustice would intervene in his literary career.
In 1790, revolutionary France adopted a remarkable legal provision: the descendants of French people expelled because of their religious beliefs could recover their French nationality if they settled in the country and took the civic oath. The law imposed no limit on how many generations had passed since the exile, which meant that the state recognised the right of return even for people who had never seen the land of their ancestors.
And so, around 1880, Cherbuliez, already an established novelist and political commentator, took advantage of precisely this opportunity. He did not need to invent French ancestry: it was enough to prove the ancestry that royal policy had once forced his family to carry abroad.
Only a year later, he was elected to the French Academy. But before that, he had also stood as a candidate for the vacant seat of the celebrated lexicographer Émile Littré, losing to Louis Pasteur. Thus, a single academic contest brought into competition a writer whose ancestors had been driven out of France and a scientist whose name is now familiar to almost every child.
Particularly intriguing is the way Ernest Renan welcomed the new academician in 1882. According to him, Cherbuliez had been French by law for only two years, but had long been French through his talent. The compliment is exquisite, although it also reveals the characteristic nineteenth-century conviction that France had the right to claim as its own anyone sufficiently talented who wrote in its language.
I find the entire story magnificently European. A monarchy expels a family because of its beliefs, a revolution recognises the right of its descendants to return, and an academy admits the heir of those exiles among the guardians of the French language. Between these three events lie almost two centuries, several political regimes, and quite a few changing definitions of who belongs to a nation.
There is also a detail that lends this story a particular irony. Cherbuliez was born in Geneva, studied in Paris, Bonn, and Berlin, knew European political culture from within, and wrote in French long before the French state officially recognised him as one of its citizens.
As my coffee grows cold beside the Black Sea, I find myself thinking that Louis XIV could hardly have foreseen such a development when he decided to make religious unity more important than freedom of conscience.
It turned out that a state may expel a person, but it does not always succeed in expelling his descendants from history.
And in the case of Victor Cherbuliez, France ultimately had not only to welcome him back, but also to offer him a seat among its Immortals.
Pasteur, of course, had received the other one.

One should understand Islam is a religious government entity. Its sole purpose is to have the whole world under its influence. But the problem within Islam it is divided within itself. So lets look at its own sources explain itself. 
Classical Islamic doctrine, drawn from the Quran, Hadith, and historical jurisprudence, the religion is understood as a complete system (din) that integrates belief, law (Sharia), and political order, with the stated aim of Islam becoming dominant over all other systems. This is not a modern invention or fringe view; it appears in core texts and the classical division of the world into dar al-Islam (territory under Islamic rule and Sharia) and dar al-Harb (territory of war/outside Islamic sovereignty). Early jurists developed these categories in the context of the rapid 7th–8th century expansions after Muhammad’s death.⁠Wikipedia 
Textual basis for global prevalence Key Quranic verses state the purpose of Muhammad’s mission in terms of supremacy: •  Quran 9:33 (also 48:28 and 61:9): “It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although they who associate others with Allah dislike it.”⁠Quran Traditional tafsirs (such as Ibn Kathir) link this to Hadith in which Muhammad says Allah showed him the earth’s east and west and that the rule of his community would reach that far, and that Islam would enter every house of mud or hair, bringing honor to some and humiliation to others. 
See ⁠Quran: https://t.co/L0KLiiG07A Related commands include fighting until there is no more fitnah (often interpreted in classical sources as opposition to Islam or disorder) and “the religion is entirely for Allah” (Quran 8:39), and the verse on fighting People of the Book until they pay the jizya in a state of submission (Quran 9:29). Classical practice offered non-Muslims (initially Jews and Christians, later expanded) dhimmi status under Islamic rule rather than immediate forced conversion in all cases, but the territorial and legal supremacy of Islam was the goal. The ultimate horizon in much traditional thought is the worldwide prevalence of Islam, sometimes tied to eschatological figures (Mahdi, return of Jesus as a Muslim). Spiritual goals exist alongside this—submission to Allah, a “soul at peace,” paradise—but the political-legal dimension of expanding and enforcing the system is explicit in classical sources. 
Historical pattern and the political dimension Muhammad’s own career in Medina combined religious leadership with political and military authority. After his death (632 CE), the Rashidun, Umayyad, and Abbasid caliphates rapidly expanded the territory under Islamic rule across the Middle East, North Africa, Spain, and into Asia. This matches the classical expectation that Muslim rulers had a duty to enlarge dar al-Islam. Modern Islamist movements (e.g., those seeking a restored caliphate) treat this as a continuing obligation; many ordinary Muslims do not actively pursue military expansion and emphasize dawah (invitation) or personal practice instead. Islam is therefore accurately described as a religion whose classical form produces and expects a political order under Sharia, not merely a private spiritual path. It is not a single “government entity” today (there is no unified caliphate), but the ideal of unified Islamic governance remains a reference point for some. 
Internal divisions
I have noted the divisions and they need to be understood. The primary split is Sunni (~85–90% of Muslims) versus Shia (~10–15%), originating in the succession crisis after Muhammad’s death: most accepted election or selection of leaders from the community/companions (leading to the caliphate), while the Shia (“party of Ali”) insisted on Ali and his descendants (the Imamate).⁠History This crystallized with the Battle of Karbala (680 CE) {Personal note: Which I believe has restarted in some sense today drawing the whole world into its battle} and the martyrdom of Husayn. Further splits exist within both (Twelver, Ismaili, Zaydi Shia; various Sunni schools and movements such as Salafi/Wahhabi, Sufi orders). Historically these have produced civil wars, competing claims to authority, and modern conflicts (Iraq, Syria, Yemen, etc.). The divisions have repeatedly undermined the ideal of a single ummah under one political authority, which is itself a classical aspiration. 
Summary for clear expression 
A concise way to state the classical position, grounded in the sources above: Islam’s foundational texts and jurisprudence present it as the final, universal revelation whose purpose includes making the religion of truth prevail over all others; spiritually through submission to Allah and politically through the expansion of territory and law under Sharia (dar al-Islam). Non-Muslims may live under it in subordinate status in the traditional model. Internal sectarian divisions over leadership and authority have been a persistent obstacle to realizing unified political expression of that goal. Interpretations vary widely among contemporary Muslims: some treat the political expansion as historical or spiritualized, others as obligatory. The classical textual and historical record is unambiguous on the aspiration for prevalence. text:
Stronger Than a City

We usually think of strength as power on the outside: big muscles, a loud voice, the one who wins every argument. But some of the strongest people you'll ever meet are the ones who feel the rage rising and choose not to let it rule them.

Scripture puts it this way:

"He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city." (Proverbs 16:32, KJV)

Anger left unchecked is never small for long. Jesus warned that hatred in the heart is where murder begins. It starts as replaying what someone did to you, then wishing them harm, then words that cut, and sometimes hands that hurt. The same is true of lust. A spirit that isn't ruled by God gets ruled by whatever feeling shouts the loudest.

Maybe you've already said things you can't take back. Maybe your temper has scared the people you love, or the anger turns inward and you hurt yourself. Hear this: Jesus is not done with you. He took the punishment for every angry word and every dark thought on the cross, and He offers you a new heart with His Spirit inside, the Spirit whose fruit includes self-control.

Here's how to let Him rule your spirit:

1. Name what's underneath. Anger often covers hurt, fear, or shame. Tell God what's really going on.
2. Build in a pause. When you feel it rising, step away, breathe, and pray before you speak or type.
3. Refuse to rehearse revenge. When the replay starts, pray a blessing over that person instead, even if it's through gritted teeth.
4. Make things right. Apologize where you've hurt someone, without excuses.
5. If you've ever thought about hurting someone or yourself, tell a trusted believer or a counselor today. You don't have to carry that alone.

Pray: "Lord, my anger has ruled me too long. Rule my spirit with Your peace. Make me slow to anger and quick to forgive, like You. In Jesus' name, Amen."

The quiet strength of a surrendered heart is greater than any army.

text:
But at the camp, Macnaghten refused to acknowledge the seriousness of the situation, and Elphinstone decided to wait until the next morning before taking any action. By then, an estimated 50,000 had joined the rebellion.

Over the next several days, the rebels captured other British outposts, including those containing the food and water stores - a stash that could have fed the army for three years. Within the camp, however, there was only two days worth of supplies. The Afghans surrounded the camp and, from the high ground overlooking it, began sniping at the now-starving British soldiers. Finally, the British attempted a foray out of camp to drive the Afghans from the high ground, but it ended with more than 300 men killed and nothing accomplished. Soon after, Akbar Khan arrived to take command of the rebels; he tightened the siege on the camp.

The British now decided that their only hope was to arrange with Akbar Khan to let them withdraw from Kabul and go back to India. A meeting was set up between Akbar and Macnaghten at which Akbar promised to allow the British to retreat unharmed through the Khyber passes and to provide them with food and an escort. In return, Dost Mohammad would be released to reclaim the throne. Macnaghten tried to cut a secret deal with Akbar to betray some of the other warlords, but Akbar revealed this duplicity to his fellow chiefs. At another meeting to supposedly work out the details, Akbar’s men seized Macnaghten, a scufﬂe broke out, and he and the other Englishmen were killed. Once again, the British made no attempt to avenge their slain ofﬁcers.
. . .

On January 6, 1842, with snow a foot deep on the ground, the British departed. There were about 3,800 Indian troops, 700 European soldiers, and 12,000 to 14,000 camp followers. The escort that Akbar Khan had promised to ensure their safe passage was nowhere to be found. They had about 90 miles to travel to reach the British fort at Jalalabad.

Shortly after leaving, Elphinstone ordered a halt, then couldn’t decide whether or not to continue. Tribesmen began to snipe at the column, and most of the cannons, as well as the meager supplies, were abandoned in the resulting panic. Night fell, bringing with it freezing temperatures. The column had covered just 5 of the 90 miles.

The next morning, the column crawled forward again under a constant hail of ﬁre. Elphinstone called another halt at the entrance to Khord Pass. Akbar Khan sent a message saying that if the British would provide him with hostages, he would arrange for them to get through the pass safely. Astonishingly, Elphinstone accepted the offer at face value and waited all day to meet Akbar.

Pushing on, the survivors ﬁnally reached the pass, only to ﬁnd that Akbar Khan had delayed them so that hordes of tribesmen could gather in the narrow conﬁnes of the pass and subject the column to withering ﬁre. Crammed together, the British and their followers were mowed down; 3,000 were killed. The survivors set off again the next morning, but after only a mile, Elphinstone halted again. This time, many ignored him. The remaining wives and children of the ofﬁcers were turned over to the mercy of Akbar Khan. The number of soldiers was probably fewer than 1,000 by this point, and safety was still 70 miles away.

🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran's captured "spy drone" looks like a real American target drone, and it may be a sign the US is already poking Iran's air defenses before the big strike

What's found in the IRGC's footage:

- The aircraft looks like an MQM-170C Outlaw, a cheap US drone normally used as a flying target for training, nearly 11 feet long with a 16-foot wingspan and up to 8 hours in the air

- It has a camera-style window on its nose used for navigation, and it's missing the bright orange paint target drones usually carry

- The IRGC says it took control with electronic warfare west of the Strait of Hormuz and landed it intact while it was scouting coastal air defenses; no proof offered for either claim

- CENTCOM says the IRGC "repeatedly lied out of desperation," but did not deny losing one of these drones

- In June the Army awarded Griffon Aerospace nearly $68 million for a new Outlaw version, and the announcement first said it was “in support of Operation Epic Fury” before that line disappeared; another $133 million order followed in August

- Last month Iran recovered a US underwater drone intact, which Washington later confirmed lost to a malfunction

You might be asking why a cheap drone matters so much... strip out the propaganda and both sides still gave something away.

If the drone is real, the Pentagon has been buying these by the hundreds of millions for this war and flying them close enough to Iran’s coast to lose one. 

And if Iran really pulled it down with electronic jamming instead of a missile, the IRGC just showed Washington the trick it plans to use when the bigger drones and bombers come after Nov. 3.

Either way, the fight over Hormuz is already being played out in cheap aircraft nobody admits to flying.
